correctness.rationale: Debarre-Manivel's line specialization expresses the count as the coefficient of \((1-x)\prod_i q_{d_i}(x)\), where \(q_d(x)=\prod_{j=0}^d((d-j)+jx)\). If any \(d_i\) is even, the endpoint factors contribute even constants and every coefficient is even. If all degrees are odd, modulo two each factor is one for even \(j\) and \(x\) for odd \(j\), so \(q_{d_i}\equiv x^{(d_i+1)/2}\); the zero-dimensional condition makes the product \(x^{n-1}\), giving odd target coefficient. Complex conjugation then pairs nonreal lines. A fresh independent exact coefficient replay found no discrepancy in 87 admissible cases through \(n=10\).
correctness.risk: The geometric real-line conclusion needs the stated general/transverse zero-dimensional setting.

Under the audit rule that direct corollaries of stronger exact formulas are covered, the all-multidegree parity reduction is not original.

final_claim: For a general complete intersection with zero-dimensional Fano scheme of lines, the finite complex line count is odd exactly when every defining degree is odd; for a general real such complete intersection, all-odd degrees therefore force at least one real line.
limitations: General transverse zero-dimensional Fano schemes of lines only.
Parity only; no exact count or lower bound on the number of real lines beyond existence.
